1) mental status change is the most common symptom associated with the ordering of urine tests in LTCF residents; 2) the majority of urine tests ordered are not associated with symptoms of UTI; and 3) antibiotic treatment was often empirically prescribed despite negative results of urine testing.

(1) Mental status change was the symptom most commonly documented in the medical record as a reason to order urine testing, (2) mental status change was also the symptom most commonly associated with the ordering of empiric antimicrobial therapy, and (3) mental status change, along with other common symptoms, such as confusion and agitation, was associated with the ordering, but not with the continuation, of inappropriate antimicrobial therapy for UTIs.
